content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements in the first 3–5 days of the forecast horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model reacts too slowly; delay in upward correction.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment volatility, especially when sentiment swings sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects after sharp price spikes, leading to premature retracement.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently underestimates late-period price peaks (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is positive for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast floor slightly to avoid underestimating downside risk.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment history when price is near recent 10-day average — apply sentiment weighting to adjust mean.
